title: DeviceChain — Edge Agent
description: The DeviceChain edge agent on the sites you run: whether each agent is connected to the cloud, how much it is holding back while the link is down, what it forwards and what it refuses or loses. Import this file into the Grafana that scrapes your agents; it is not installed with an instance. Start with the tiles: lost events must stay at zero.

panels.title: Agents reporting
panels.description: Agents your Prometheus is scraping right now. If a site you expect is missing, its agent or the relay that exposes its metrics is down, or its metrics port is disabled.

panels.title: Agents disconnected
panels.description: Agents whose link to the cloud is down. They keep accepting device data and buffer it on the box; the backlog panels show how far behind each one is. Above zero: check the site's network and the cloud MQTT endpoint.

panels.title: Oldest buffered event
panels.description: Age of the oldest event any selected agent still holds, the main backlog signal. It stays near zero while the link is healthy. Yellow after 5 minutes, red after an hour: the site has been cut off for that long, and the buffer is filling toward its limit.

panels.title: Fullest buffer
panels.description: How full the most-loaded agent's buffer is, as a share of its configured size. At 100% the oldest buffered events are discarded to make room. Yellow from 70%, red from 90%: restore the link, or raise the buffer size.

panels.title: Events lost to overflow, over the range
panels.description: Oldest buffered events discarded because the buffer was full. Any value above zero is real data loss. Restore the link and raise the buffer size.

panels.title: Events refused, over the range
panels.description: Events the platform refused for a gateway, plus events the agent would not forward. Any value above zero needs attention: see Refused and rejected events below for the reason.

panels.title: Open local listeners
panels.description: Agents whose local device port requires no credential. Zero open listeners is the safe posture; an open listener is valid on a trusted network but is easy to leave that way by mistake.

panels.title: Agents
panels.description: One row per agent. Connected is the live link state. Oldest event is how far behind the agent is. Buffer is how full its buffer is. Lost and Refused count events over the selected time range. Local credential shows whether the device port requires one.

panels.title: Cloud link, per agent
panels.description: 1 while the agent's link to the cloud is up, 0 while it is down. A line that keeps dropping to 0 is a flapping link; a line stuck at 0 is a site that is cut off and buffering.

panels.title: Publishes waiting for the cloud
panels.description: Events sent to the cloud and not yet acknowledged, at most 64 per agent. Staying at 64 while a backlog drains is normal; staying at 64 with nothing draining means the cloud is not acknowledging.

panels.title: Age of the oldest buffered event
panels.description: How far behind each agent is in wall-clock time. Near zero when the link is healthy; it grows by one second per second while the site is cut off. This is the primary backlog signal.

panels.title: Buffered events
panels.description: Events captured on the box and not yet forwarded. They are forwarded in order when the link returns.

panels.title: Buffer used
panels.description: Bytes held in each agent's buffer against its configured maximum. When the used line reaches the limit line, the oldest events start to be discarded.

panels.title: Buffer fill
panels.description: Share of the buffer in use per agent. At 100% data is being lost; the Events lost tile and the panel below count it.

panels.title: Events lost to overflow
panels.description: Oldest buffered events discarded per second to stay within the buffer size. Any standing rate is data loss. The count does not reset when an agent restarts.

panels.title: Events in and out
panels.description: Events read from the buffer for forwarding and events the cloud acknowledged, per second, across the selected agents. Received above forwarded for long means a backlog is building.

panels.title: Forwarded per agent
panels.description: Events the cloud acknowledged per second, for each agent. A site that goes flat while its devices are active has a problem between the box and the cloud.

panels.title: Forward attempts that failed
panels.description: Forward attempts that failed per second. The event stays buffered and is sent again, so a brief rate during a reconnect is normal; a standing rate with the link up means the cloud is rejecting or timing out.

panels.title: Refused events, by reason
panels.description: Events refused per second. not_gateway_child: the device is not assigned to this gateway, or does not exist. gateway_self and invalid_device_token: the agent would not forward it. other: a reason this agent version does not know. Refused events are kept in the local dead-letter file while the agent still holds them.

panels.title: Refused events kept or unmatched
panels.description: Refused events written to the local dead-letter file, and refusals whose event was no longer on the box (the platform's failed-events record has its payload), per second.

panels.title: Events discarded on the box
panels.description: Per second: events dropped for a malformed subject, device publishes for a different tenant or instance than the agent is configured for (not forwarded), and credential members removed from event bodies before forwarding. A standing rate on the first three is a misconfigured device; the last one means a device should stop sending credentials.

panels.title: Local credential required
panels.description: 1 when the agent's local device port requires a credential, 0 when it is open. Alert on 0 where you expect 1.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident memory of each agent process. A steady climb with a flat event rate is a leak worth reporting.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used by each agent process, in cores.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines in each agent process. A steady climb means something is leaking.

panels.title: Open files
panels.description: Open file descriptors against the process limit. The buffer and the local device connections each hold some; approaching the limit stops new device connections.
